result.scientific_strategy:
## 052b98fa-ee96-41c6-ae7e-1c2ad99cfc0a / Scientific strategy

**Current synthesis:** The campaign objective is at least 98% success on the official two-joint-arm reach-and-hold task. The first fresh PPO run learned substantial task behavior and reached 97.5% (195/200) on the development task-reference panel at checkpoint-105472, but its later checkpoints fell to 95.5% and 92.0% while training reward and proxy success continued to rise. Checkpoint-105472 is therefore the strongest current policy evidence, close to but below the objective, and the campaign has not established terminal readiness.

**Lessons and limits:** Training reward and proxy success are useful learning-dynamics signals but did not predict the ordering of the measured late checkpoints. The raw log shows steadily improving training proxies from 90,112 through 120,832 steps, while the shared task-reference panel shows a real behavioral decline; this identifies a proxy/performance discrepancy without identifying its cause. The five failures of checkpoint-105472 all truncated at 500 steps, but the fixed development panel is distinct from the official panel and the single fresh run cannot establish run-to-run variability or causal attribution. Sources: `research/scenario.md`, `research/brief.md`, `research/research_state.json`, `research/results.jsonl`, `research/training_logs/052b98fa-ee96-41c6-ae7e-1c2ad99cfc0a/experiment-1-attempt-1.log`, and the three experiment-1 task-reference artifacts under `research/evaluations/052b98fa-ee96-41c6-ae7e-1c2ad99cfc0a/`.

**Open questions:** It remains unresolved whether the late degradation reflects PPO update dynamics, reward or termination incentives, target-distribution differences, run-specific variation, or another aspect of the scientific recipe. It is also unresolved whether the five residual failures of checkpoint-105472 can be reduced without sacrificing its measured robustness, and whether development-panel performance transfers to the official assessment.
